{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-ks-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"6632d6eb7caa7761faa73fe98ce9661f6ae6d1da26bbf48b994c10398b0f612d","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-ks-class-c:lineage:41","source_registry_sha256":"c7fb2073a9e8bb6a73d0151458fe04991b703d84f882b00a01bedfcea433c383","source_liveness_sha256":"94328be42cc10cf86af8e486b41bc40c72c45e4700d27b9b46d1f3d2feac7bb6"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Sharing the road","heading":"C2 — Sharing the road","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Sharing the road

FACT_ID: sec09-R01 | anchor: A85
For an approaching siren or flashing emergency lights, move right, stop parallel close to the curb or edge, and keep intersections clear. [A85]
Source: [A85 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec09-R02 | anchor: A85
After an emergency vehicle passes, check behind for others and rejoin traffic only when safe. [A85]
Source: [A85 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec09-R03 | anchor: A85
In its emergency-vehicle passage instructions, the handbook requires staying at least 500 feet from the emergency vehicle. [A85]
Source: [A85 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec09-R04 | anchor: A85
Stop for an emergency vehicle entering or leaving its garage with lights flashing until it is safely clear of the path. [A85]
Source: [A85 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec09-R05 | anchor: A85
At an emergency scene, follow the directions of law enforcement and emergency-service personnel. [A85]
Source: [A85 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec09-R06 | anchor: A85
For a police stop, pull right and as far outside traffic as safely possible for both the driver and officer. [A85]
Source: [A85 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec09-R07 | anchor: A85
During a traffic stop, switch off the engine and distracting audio or devices, activate hazard lights and lower the window to communicate. [A85]
Source: [A85 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec09-R08 | anchor: A85
At night during a traffic stop, turn on the interior light so the officer can see inside. [A85]
Source: [A85 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec09-R09 | anchor: A85
Remain calm with seat belts fastened during a traffic stop, and ask passengers to do the same. [A85]
Source: [A85 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec09-R10 | anchor: A85
Keep hands on the wheel and minimize movements during a police stop. [A85]
Source: [A85 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec09-R11 | anchor: A85
When asked for license, insurance or registration, tell the officer where the documents are and reach slowly while keeping one hand on the wheel. [A85]
Source: [A85 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec09-R12 | anchor: A85
Remain inside during a traffic stop unless asked to exit, and answer the officer clearly. [A85]
Source: [A85 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec09-R13 | anchor: A85
Do not flee law enforcement; police pursuits create serious crash risks. [A85]
Source: [A85 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec09-R14 | anchor: A85
When approaching a stationary same-direction emergency vehicle with flashing lights, including a tow or recovery vehicle, leave the adjacent lane if safe and possible; otherwise slow appropriately for traffic, weather and road conditions. [A85]
Source: [A85 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec09-R15 | anchor: A85
Large vehicles maneuver less readily, have larger blind spots and need longer stopping and acceleration distances and more turning space than cars. [A85]
Source: [A85 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec09-R16 | anchor: A86
The No-Zone consists of blind areas at the front, rear and sides of large trucks or buses. [A86]
Source: [A86 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec09-R17 | anchor: A86
A truck's right-side blind area starts behind the cab and can extend along the truck's length. [A86]
Source: [A86 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec09-R18 | anchor: A86
The handbook uses inability to see the truck driver's face in a side mirror as a warning that the driver cannot see the following vehicle. [A86]
Source: [A86 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec09-R19 | anchor: A86
Avoid remaining beside a large vehicle longer than needed because a lane change or swerve can create a collision. [A86]
Source: [A86 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec09-R20 | anchor: A86
The handbook's loaded-truck example at 55 mph, with good tires, correctly adjusted brakes and ideal conditions, requires at least 335 feet to stop. [A86]
Source: [A86 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec09-R21 | anchor: A86
After passing a large vehicle, wait until its full front appears in the rearview mirror before moving ahead of it, and maintain speed. [A86]
Source: [A86 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec09-R22 | anchor: A86
Large-vehicle rear blind spots can extend as much as 200 feet; close following also blocks the following driver's forward view. [A86]
Source: [A86 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec09-R23 | anchor: A86
Follow large vehicles with room to react and a position visible in their side mirrors. [A86]
Source: [A86 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec09-R24 | anchor: A86
When possible, avoid the right lane near truck weigh stations where slow trucks reenter faster traffic. [A86]
Source: [A86 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec09-R25 | anchor: A87
A truck or bus may swing left before a right turn and need space from more than one lane. [A87]
Source: [A87 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-R26 | anchor: A87
Do not squeeze between a turning truck or bus and the curb; wait for its turn to finish before turning. [A87]
Source: [A87 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-R27 | anchor: A87
When meeting an opposing truck, leave as much right-side clearance as possible to reduce sideswipe and turbulence risks. [A87]
Source: [A87 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-R28 | anchor: A87
If uncertain about an opposing truck or bus's speed, do not turn left across its path. [A87]
Source: [A87 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-R29 | anchor: A87
Stop behind intersection stop lines, which also preserve turning room for large vehicles. [A87]
Source: [A87 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-R30 | anchor: A87
Do not cut off a truck to reach a turn, exit or single-lane work area. [A87]
Source: [A87 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-R31 | anchor: A87
Runaway ramps on long descents are reserved for large vehicles that cannot stop or have lost control; do not stop or park there. [A87]
Source: [A87 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-R32 | anchor: A87
A stopped transit bus may hide pedestrians or be about to reenter traffic; watch boarding and exiting passengers. [A87]
Source: [A87 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-R33 | anchor: A87
A transit safety zone protects people boarding, leaving or waiting for rail transit; do not drive through or park in the zone. [A87]
Source: [A87 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-R34 | anchor: A87
Pass a transit safety zone only when safe and at no more than 10 mph. [A87]
Source: [A87 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-R35 | anchor: A87
Without a safety zone, stop behind the nearest trolley or light-rail door or platform while people board or leave, and wait until they reach safety. [A87]
Source: [A87 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-R36 | anchor: A87
Do not pass a moving or stopped trolley or light-rail vehicle on the left except on a one-way street, where tracks prevent right-side passing, or when directed by a traffic officer. [A87]
Source: [A87 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-R37 | anchor: A87
Let an approaching trolley or light-rail vehicle pass before turning across its path. [A87]
Source: [A87 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-R38 | anchor: A87
Buildings, trees and other obstructions can restrict a rail operator's view. [A87]
Source: [A87 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-R39 | anchor: A88
When sharing a roadway with a trolley or light-rail vehicle, preserve safe following space. [A88]
Source: [A88 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec09-R40 | anchor: A88
An orange-and-red reflective or fluorescent triangle on the rear of a slow vehicle indicates travel below 25 mph. [A88]
Source: [A88 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec09-R41 | anchor: A88
Approach slow-moving vehicles cautiously and pass only when safe. [A88]
Source: [A88 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec09-R42 | anchor: A88
Rural farm equipment may cross roads or occupy more than one lane because of its width. [A88]
Source: [A88 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec09-R43 | anchor: A88
Farm equipment may lack turn signals and swing left before turning right; do not assume its initial movement predicts the turn. [A88]
Source: [A88 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0088]

Misconceptions: A cyclist or motorcyclist may need a full lane; another rider's signal does not prove a turn; a truck's leftward setup can precede a right turn; transit and school-bus rules differ.
Mnemonics: Editorial cue: identify the user, protect the gap, confirm the path. It adds no road-user entitlement or legal exception.
Glossary: Distinguish sharrow, bike lane, bike route, No-Zone, move-over response, pedestrian safety zone and slow-moving triangle using the source-bound blocks.
Dynamic facts: Edition-bound legal definitions and distances require issuer refresh. Undated statistics, red-signal procedure, sign-image geometry and contradictory instructions remain typed debt; no current-law clearance is implied.

FACT_ID: sec09-R44 | anchor: A88
Farm machines commonly travel below 25 mph; use caution when passing them. [A88]
Source: [A88 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec09-R45 | anchor: A88
Animal-drawn vehicles share road rights and traffic-rule duties with motor vehicles. [A88]
Source: [A88 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec09-R46 | anchor: A88
Animal-drawn vehicles normally travel about 5 to 8 mph and may be slower while hauling farm equipment or crossing intersections. [A88]
Source: [A88 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec09-R47 | anchor: A88
A large load can obstruct an animal-drawn vehicle driver's rear view; pass with extra care. [A88]
Source: [A88 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec09-R48 | anchor: A88
Do not honk or rev the engine near animal-drawn traffic because a frightened horse can cause a crash. [A88]
Source: [A88 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec09-R49 | anchor: A88
Anticipate animal-drawn vehicles turning left into fields or driveways. [A88]
Source: [A88 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec09-R50 | anchor: A88
Horse riders should travel single file near the right edge or on a usable right shoulder, lane or path. [A88]
Source: [A88 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec09-R51 | anchor: A88
Approach or pass a ridden or led horse at a reasonable speed and distance without loud horn or engine noise. [A88]
Source: [A88 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec09-R52 | anchor: A88
A slow-vehicle driver causing others to slow should pull aside when safe to let them pass. [A88]
Source: [A88 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0088]
